messages:
nick: FYI customer RFP: fully air-gapped POC. no network egress allowed after install. they want monthly security patches but offline-only delivery. asking for a clear runbook + ballpark uplift.

anna: got it. do they expect us to physically ship media or will they pull from an SFTP drop in their DMZ?

nick: they prefer USB/SSD handoff to their SOC team. no remote console access except during a supervised maintenance window.

li: tech lead here 12. Constraints: 1) any model artifact >4GB might require sharding for USB FAT32 compatibility, 2) signed manifests needed, 3) we need to provide a deterministic build artifact so their verifier can reproduce checksum.

ops_beth: ops POV: offline installs increase human ops. suggest staging import step: 1) dry-run validation that bundle unpacks & checksums, 2) preflight runs of config validator, 3) offline integrity tests. If they want monthly patches we'll need a repeatable process.

security_ron: security asks: supply chain attestation, chain-of-trust for signing keys, proof we don't phone-home, and an allowlist of any outbound endpoints if temporary egress required. we also need to sign an SLA clause for incident escalation under sealed mode.

nick: what's the typical uplift for handling sealed/offline POCs?

anna: typical commercial: one-time POC service fee + per-bundle handling. e.g., $4-8k one-time for packaging+labwork + $750 per physical bundle (media, checksums, signing, QA). Alternatively, a labor-based model: X eng-days for package + on-call support hours.

li: engineering estimate: initial airgap kit (bundle tooling, manifest schema, signer infra) ~6 eng-days to produce reproducible pipeline, then ~0.5-1 eng-day per bundle for validation + signing. monthly cadence => ~6 + 6-12 eng-days first quarter, then ~2-4 eng-days ongoing per month.

ops_beth: rollback expectations? they requested "easy revert within 10 days". Clarify: are they talking image revert only or full DB rollback?

nick: customer said "system revert to previous known-good state". assume image revert only unless they confirm DB migrations.

li: agree. we can deliver image-level rollback (retain two prior bundle versions on node) and a restoration playbook. DB migrations will require explicit migration scripts that are reversible; otherwise we declare migrations as one-way in the SOW.

security_ron: HSM/KMS: they want to bring their own HSM for signing. We support detached signing via a CI job that consumes a remote signing API. Need to document KMS integration checklist and token exchange.

anna: telemetry question: they want 0 telemetry. we can ship a 'no-telemetry' runtime build but support will be limited. propose a 'debug-key' procedure: customer can enable ephemeral egress for troubleshooting under supervised conditions and we bill for remote debug time.

nick: can we include an identity proof in the bundle so their compliance team can validate it offline?

li: yes. include a signed provenance.json with build-id, builder-hash, model-hash, base-image-id, and signatures. provide verification script they can run locally.

ops_beth: media checklist for USB delivery in runbook: redact PII, encrypt payload with customer-provided key, include SHA256 and ed25519 signatures, include import dry-run command, and a step-by-step fallback plan if import fails. recommend portable SSD for >32GB models.

anna: timeline: we can produce initial POC kit + runbook in 8 business days if we prioritize. packaging automation would add 2 weeks but reduce per-bundle time thereafter.

nick: next actions: @li + @ops_beth create a 1-2 page runbook + sample manifest and a short cost note. @security_ron draft KMS/HSM checklist and addendum language. I'll share with the customer tomorrow.

salesbot: task created: "airgap-poc-runbook-draft" assigned to li,ops_beth,security_ron due_in:48h

li: will upload a sample manifest and a checksum verifier script to the deal folder by EOD.

ops_beth: i'll draft the media handling section and include the dry-run commands.

security_ron: drafting addendum; will propose a minimal set of attestations and an opt-in "ephemeral debug" clause.
